key_insight: Agentic RSR connects scene reconstruction and robot policy learning into one loop, so the simulated workspace matches the real task and the learned policy can act using real-robot observations. In simple terms: it tries to make the sim look and behave like the real world in a task-aware way.
problem_solved: Most real-to-sim-to-real pipelines treat environment reconstruction and policy training separately, which can cause a mismatch between what is simulated and what the robot can actually perceive and do. This paper addresses the challenge of building task-relevant simulations and execution-grounded policies from the same real-world manipulation data.
method: Use a workspace video, task description, and known robot model to reconstruct a task-relevant simulation of the real scene.
Develop robot policies in simulation that are grounded in the observations and actions available to the physical robot.
Link reconstruction, policy learning, and real-robot execution through the same manipulation task to reduce sim-to-real gap.
impact: This matters for AI/ML practitioners because it provides a more unified pathway from real-world data to deployable robot behavior. It can improve transfer reliability in manipulation tasks by aligning what is simulated, learned, and executed.

paper_title: Agentic RSR: Real-to-Sim-to-Real through Scene Reconstruction and Execution-Grounded Robot Policies
paper_authors: Yihan Li, Yating Feng, Shengjiu Sun, Jianing Chen, Hao Ren
